title: Heated Slippers and Bed Foot Warmers: Warm Feet Without Cranking the Thermostat
subtitle: A plain-English look at battery heated slippers and under-the-sheet foot warmers, what they cost, and what they cannot do.
excerpt: Cold feet can make a whole evening miserable. Here is how heated slippers and bed foot warmers work, what to check before you buy, and two products to consider, though neither is confirmed as a budget pick.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Some people can be comfortable everywhere except their feet. The living room feels fine, the sweater is doing its job, and yet the toes stay cold. At bedtime it can be worse, lying awake waiting for the sheets to warm up.

Turning up the heat for the whole house to fix two cold feet is an expensive answer. Heated slippers and bed foot warmers aim the warmth right where it is wanted. They can make a thoughtful gift for a parent or grandparent, as long as you pick the right kind for the person and the home. If you are after something for the lap and shoulders, our guide to heated throws covers those. This one is all about feet.
How They Work: Your Main Options

There are three common approaches, and each suits a different kind of day. One note on sources: the general description of how heated slippers work comes from a single Popular Science roundup last updated in November 2024, so models and prices may have changed since then.

These look like regular cozy slippers but have heating panels inside. According to Popular Science, some use a battery module, much like heated socks, while others have an internal heating pad that charges by USB, the same kind of cable many phones use. You charge them fully, unplug them, and walk around in them. The trade-off is runtime: once the battery runs down, they need recharging. The Volt Heat slipper below lists up to 12 hours on low and about 4.5 hours on high.

Popular Science also covers separate microwave or battery foot warmers that you slip inside slippers you already own. That may suit someone who would rather keep a favorite pair. We have not looked at specific products in this style, so check each one's instructions.

These are flat electric pads that go under the fitted sheet at the foot of the bed. The Sunbeam pad below is corded, so it needs an outlet and a cord near the bed. It is not something you wear, so it only helps at bedtime. Auto-off helps, but a corded warmer under the covers is not a fall-safe or worry-free choice for everyone, so think about the person's mobility and where the cord will run.

items: Price. Heated slippers can cost a lot. The one slipper with a confirmed price here is $169.95, roughly four times the price of a heated throw, so it is not a budget pick. We could not confirm a lower-priced heated slipper.
Battery life on low and high. High heat drains a battery much faster, so check both numbers and think about how long the person actually sits each evening.
Replacement batteries. Popular Science notes that batteries can be proprietary and costly to replace, so they may be expensive. Ask before you buy.
A good, grippy sole. Heated soles may not grip well on slick floors. The Volt slipper has a rubber outsole, but check grip for anyone at risk of falling.
Easy on and off. The Volt slipper has a side zipper, which some people may find easier than a snug pull-on style.
Sizes. The Volt page lists only a few sizes, says limited sizes are available and offers a notify-me option, so check sizes before any gift-giving deadline.
Simple controls and auto-off. For bed warmers, look for a controller with clear settings and an automatic shut-off, and read the maker's instructions for use.
Cord placement. A plug-in warmer needs an outlet nearby and a cord that will not cross a walking path at night.
Warranty and returns. The Sunbeam pad lists a 3-year limited warranty. Check the return policy on any product before ordering.

sections.content: Setting Them Up and Using Them Well

For battery slippers, follow the maker's charging instructions, and consider writing the steps on a card in large print if you are giving them as a gift. Remember the battery figures: low heat lasts much longer than high. Keep the charger in one handy spot so recharging becomes routine.

For a bed foot warmer, follow the manufacturer's instructions for placement, cord routing and when to switch it on. Check the care label before washing. The Sunbeam pad has a 100% polyester cover; the notes list hand washing, or machine washing after a 15-minute pre-soak.

Heated footwear and foot warmers are comfort items, not medical treatments. Our caution about numbness is a general one, not drawn from a safety source such as the CPSC, FDA or Consumer Reports, none of which we consulted. If someone has numbness or reduced feeling in their feet, including from neuropathy, Raynaud's or poor circulation, they may not notice when something gets too hot, so ask their doctor before buying. And a heated slipper is still a slipper: if balance is a concern, grip matters more than warmth.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: Warm feet can turn a long winter evening into a pleasant one. Think about where the cold bothers them most, in the armchair or under the covers, and choose from there. A little planning on size, grip and charging goes a long way toward a gift they will actually use.

products.name: GEN VI Indoor/Outdoor Rechargeable Heated Slippers
products.blurb: A premium gift, not a budget pick, for someone who wants warmth while moving around the house, with heat panels on the top and bottom of the foot, a side zipper and a rubber sole. The page says they can be worn outdoors; battery life is up to 12 hours on low or about 4.5 hours on high. Sizes run from Small (women's 5/6) to Large (women's 8.5–10 / men's up to about 9) in black only, and the page says limited sizes are available.

products.name: Twin/Full Electric Foot Warming Pad
products.blurb: Suits someone whose feet get coldest in bed: a corded 25-by-45-inch pad that goes under the fitted sheet, with three heat settings, auto-off, ETL listing and a 3-year limited warranty. Its price is unconfirmed, and auto-off does not make it a fall-safe choice for everyone.
